project.objective: When did Heinrich Dewus of Milwaukee, Wisconsin (born about 1850 in Pommerania, Germany) die, and did he and his wife Augusta have children besides the four already in the tree?

questions.question: When and where did Heinrich Dewus (born about 1850 in Pomerania, Germany; Milwaukee, Wisconsin resident) die?
questions.rationale: The death date and place of Heinrich Dewus is the first independent part of the research objective. Death records, death certificates, and obituaries for Milwaukee County in this period are well-preserved and indexed on FamilySearch and Ancestry. This question is also a partial gatekeeper for the children question: obituaries frequently name surviving children, and a death certificate may name informants who are family members.

questions.question: Did Heinrich Dewus (died 23 August 1936, Milwaukee, Wisconsin) have surviving children in 1936 beyond the four recorded in the family tree — Heinrich Charles (KJW8-43Q), Alma Friedericka Wilhelmina (9MNY-WQ1), Adela Ulricka Augusta (94F3-YQH), and Hedwig Bertha Anna (9VX4-1H3) — and if so, who were they?
questions.rationale: The research objective asked whether Heinrich Dewus and Augusta Arndt had children beyond the four in the tree. The obituary evidence (Q5SZ-SH2M) names six surviving children, four matching existing tree entries and two new ones — Walter (no surname given) and Ida Dewes. This question targets that finding directly: it is answerable from the obituary evidence at a probable tier, and Milwaukee census and birth records would corroborate and potentially extend the list. Wisconsin birth records (1882–1890), the 1900 US census, and the 1880 US census are indexed on FamilySearch for Milwaukee County.

items.rationale: Wisconsin Death Index 1820–1907 (collection 1940759, 435,208 records) is indexed and free — the highest-probability first search for a pre-1908 death. Milwaukee County began recording deaths ~1852; coverage is strong from the 1870s onward. The index provides date and may lead to the original certificate image. Try 'Dewus' and spelling variants: Dewes, Dews, Dewis, Devus.

Wisconsin Death Records 1867–1907 (collection 1803975, 184,766 records, with images) is a complementary indexed collection. It may include Milwaukee deaths not captured in collection 1940759 and provides access to the original certificate. Per loc_001: death certificates after mid-July 1897 include birthplaces of the decedent's parents — critical for confirming Pomeranian origin. Search as a supplement to pli_001.

Ancestry's Milwaukee, Wisconsin, U.S., Deaths, 1854–1911 (collection 61721) provides index and images for city-level Milwaukee death registrations that may not be fully captured in the statewide FamilySearch collections. Covers through 1911 and is the primary paid fallback. May be accessible free at a FamilySearch affiliate library.

No indexed FamilySearch collection covers Wisconsin death certificates 1908–1920 (statewide registration began 1907, compliance by 1908). MyHeritage Wisconsin Deaths fills this gap. If censuses or other records show Heinrich living past 1907, his post-1907 death certificate would include birthplace, parents' names, informant, and burial details. Execute only after census searches establish whether he survived past 1907.

Federal censuses 1880, 1900, 1910, and 1920 (1890 destroyed) establish Heinrich's presence and household composition at each decade. His presence or absence in successive censuses brackets the death window. Household members listed may reveal additional children. The 1900 census asked for year of immigration and years married, helping confirm identity. Ages given corroborate the birth year of ~1850.

Wisconsin State Censuses 1885 (col. 1443713), 1895 (col. 1443712), and 1905 (col. 1443899) fill the intercensal gaps — especially critical given the 1890 federal census was destroyed. All three are indexed and free. If Heinrich died between 1885 and 1905, his disappearance between two state censuses narrows the death year significantly. These also list all household members and may identify additional children at home.

Three Milwaukee cemeteries are indexed at FamilySearch: Holy Cross (col. 3714667, 1909–1979, 146,444 records), Pilgrim's Rest (col. 3246496, 1880–1979, 15,599 records), and Wanderer's Rest (col. 3326771, 1880–1979, 30,586 records). A burial record confirms death date and place. FindAGrave and BillionGraves also cover Milwaukee and may have entries created by descendants. Forest Home Cemetery (1850–1945) and Calvary Cemetery (1857–1979) are in the FamilySearch Catalog but not indexed — browse if needed.

Milwaukee's large German immigrant community was served by German-language newspapers. The Milwaukee Public Library holds an index to Milwaukee's German Newspapers death notices and the Milwaukee Sentinel Card Index 1880–1890 — accessible in person or via contact request. Wisconsin Necrology 1846–1944 and Milwaukee Journal Index 1915–1917 are also at MPL. Chronicling America (free) has digitized Wisconsin newspapers. FAN application: obituaries commonly list surviving children, directly informing the children question (q_002 to be selected). The newspaper is often the only record surviving for deaths in years with poor registration compliance.

Milwaukee County Register in Probate holds records from 1838. FamilySearch collection 1874190 (Probate Estate Files, 1848–1948, 1,399,485 images) is browse-only; however, the Milwaukee County General Index volumes (1838–1933, full-text searchable at FamilySearch) allow searching for 'Dewus' to find the packet number without browsing. A probate file establishes the death date when the estate was opened and names heirs — directly answering both the death date and children questions. Ancestry Wisconsin Wills and Probate Records 1800–1987 (index & images) is the paid fallback.

Heinrich was from Pomerania, a predominantly Lutheran region of Germany. Milwaukee's German Lutheran and Catholic churches kept burial registers that predate and supplement civil registration. FamilySearch Catalog holds some Milwaukee church records (e.g., Calvary Catholic Cemetery 1857–1979; Evangelical Lutheran Church of America records via Archives.com). MyHeritage Wisconsin, Archdiocese of Milwaukee Catholic Burials (1800–onward) covers Catholic burials. A church burial entry would confirm date of death and burial place and may name the officiating pastor's congregation, helping identify the family's church for further record searches. Fallback for cemetery records (pli_007) if no entry is found there.

All four known Dewus children (Alma 1882, Adela 1883, Hedwig 1885, Heinrich Charles 1889) have birth records in 'Wisconsin, Births and Christenings, 1826-1926' (collection 1708703). Walter, named in the 1936 obituary as a surviving son, should have a comparable record. His birth record would name both Heinrich Dewus and Augusta Arndt as parents — direct parentage evidence — and would fix his birth year and settle the 'Dewes' vs 'Dewus' spelling question. Search: givenName=Walter, fatherSurname=Dewus, birthPlace=Milwaukee, collectionId=1708703.

Ida, named as 'Miss Ida Dewes' in the 1936 obituary (a surviving daughter), would also appear in 'Wisconsin, Births and Christenings, 1826-1926' (collection 1708703) if born in Milwaukee. Her birth record would confirm parentage from both Heinrich and Augusta and explain the 'Dewes' surname variant (likely a phonetic or spelling variant of 'Dewus'). Search: givenName=Ida, fatherSurname=Dewus (also try Dewes), birthPlace=Milwaukee, collectionId=1708703.

The 1900 US federal census is the highest-value single census for this question: all six children named in the obituary (born 1882–1895 approximately) would be ages 5–18 in 1900 and likely still living in the parental household. A Dewus household listing all children at home would confirm the complete sibling set and confirm Augusta Arndt's role as mother. Heinrich Charles already has a 1900 Milwaukee residence fact. Search: surname=Dewus, residencePlace=Milwaukee, Wisconsin, residenceYear=1900.

The Wisconsin State Census of 1885 (collection 1443713, fully indexed, 407,138 records) provides a mid-period household snapshot. By 1885 at least three known children were present (Alma 3, Adela 1, and newborn Hedwig). Walter and Ida, if born by 1885, would also appear. This census is free on FamilySearch and more spatially granular than the federal censuses, listing full household members by name and age.

The Wisconsin State Census of 1895 (collection 1443712, 494,911 records) is a late-period snapshot between the births and the 1900 federal census. All children born by 1895 would appear. If Walter or Ida were born between 1885 and 1895, this census would capture them while the 1885 census might miss them.

The Wisconsin County Marriages collection (1803973, 199,267 records, 1836–1911) should contain the marriage record of Heinrich Dewus and Augusta Arndt. This is required for a parentage conclusion: (a) it confirms the couple married and dates their union; (b) it supplies Augusta's maiden name, which census and death records usually omit; and (c) its date relative to the children's births corroborates Heinrich as the father on all children within the marriage window. Without it, Augusta's participation as the mother of Walter and Ida rests solely on co-residence evidence. Search: surname=Dewus, givenName=Heinrich (or Henry), spouseGivenName=Augusta.

The 1880 US federal census predates all known Dewus children (oldest, Alma, was born Feb 1882). A Dewus household in 1880 would establish: (a) the marriage of Heinrich and Augusta before the children were born; (b) whether any earlier children (born before 1882 and potentially deceased by 1936) existed; (c) Augusta's age and background. This is lower priority than the 1900 census because no known children would appear, but it provides a pre-family baseline and corroborates the marriage.

conflicts.description: Heinrich Dewus death date: 23 Aug 1936 (a_003, Q5SZ-J9LG, explicit) vs. ~28 Aug 1936 (a_010, Q5SZ-SH2M, approximate — coincides with newspaper publication date)
conflicts.independence_analysis: Both assertions derive from the same underlying newspaper publication — a Milwaukee obituary printed on 28 August 1936. Q5SZ-J9LG is a focused GenealogyBank obituary entry for Henry Dewus; Q5SZ-SH2M is a combined GenealogyBank entry for 'Mr Henry Downs and Henry Dewus.' Both are indexed representations of the same 28 August 1936 newspaper issue. They are not independent: they share the same printed source and the same informant (the obituary author). Under GPS Standard 46, these related information items form one evidence unit and receive no more credibility than their strongest single member.
conflicts.weighing_analysis: Three factors differentiate the two assertions. First, precision: a_003 records an explicit, unqualified calendar date ('23 Aug 1936'); a_010 records an approximate value ('~28 Aug 1936'). When both come from the same publication, the more precise value is the stronger candidate. Second, publication-date conflation: a_010's approximate date matches the newspaper's own 28 August 1936 issue date exactly — the hallmark of an indexer substituting the publication date when no specific death date was extracted from that combined entry. This is a documented derivative-source error pattern in newspaper obituary database indexing. Third, historical plausibility: a death on 23 August with an obituary published 28 August (five days later) is entirely normal for 1930s Milwaukee; a death on the day of publication would be unusual. The defensible rationale for setting aside a_010 is derivative-source error: the indexer conflated the publication date with the death date rather than transcribing the specific date stated in the obituary text.
conflicts.resolution_rationale: The problem: Two assertions about Heinrich Dewus's death date disagree — a_003 gives 23 August 1936 (explicit, from the focused Q5SZ-J9LG entry) and a_010 gives approximately 28 August 1936 (from the combined Q5SZ-SH2M entry). The correct date is material to q_001. The conflicting evidence: Both assertions index a Milwaukee newspaper obituary published on 28 August 1936. Q5SZ-J9LG records '23 Aug 1936' without qualification. Q5SZ-SH2M records 'About 28 Aug 1936.' The informant in both cases is the obituary author — a secondary informant reporting a death they did not personally witness. Which version is more reliable: a_003 (23 Aug 1936) is preferred. Since both co-derive from the same newspaper issue, they form one evidence unit; a_003 is the stronger member because it records a specific, unqualified date rather than an approximation. An explicit date in an obituary typically reflects a statement in the text ('died August 23') rather than an inference. Why the less reliable evidence exists: a_010's approximate date coincides precisely with the newspaper's issue date (28 Aug 1936), which is the characteristic signature of a derivative-indexing artifact. In GenealogyBank/FamilySearch newspaper obituary indexing, when a combined or secondary entry does not explicitly extract a death date from the text, the publication date is sometimes recorded as an approximate death date. This is not an error in the original newspaper — the obituary text itself almost certainly stated '23 August.' The discrepancy is an indexing artifact in the derivative database, not a genuine conflict about when Dewus died.

proof_summaries.narrative_markdown:
## When and Where Did Heinrich Dewus Die?

### Summary

The evidence establishes that Heinrich Dewus — born about 1850 in Pomerania, Germany, and a long-time resident of Milwaukee, Wisconsin — **probably died on 23 August 1936 in Milwaukee, Wisconsin**.

### Sources and Evidence

**Entry for Henry Dewus (Q5SZ-J9LG).** This focused obituary index entry records Henry Dewus's death as "23 Aug 1936" in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, with an obituary published 28 August 1936.¹ The entry is a *derivative source* (a database index to an underlying newspaper) that conveys *secondary information*: the death date and place were reported to the newspaper by family informants, not observed firsthand by the reporter. The death date is recorded as an explicit, unqualified calendar date. The identity of the deceased as Heinrich Dewus (9VX4-1C3) is established by the uncommon surname *Dewus*, his known Milwaukee residence, and corroboration from the second source below. The original printed obituary, associated with image ark:/61903/1:2:QT3C-K2LH, was not examined; consulting it would confirm the stated date.

**Entry for Mr Henry Downs and Henry Dewus (Q5SZ-SH2M).** This combined obituary index entry records a death date of "About 28 Aug 1936" at 6906 W. Lloyd St., Wisconsin, for Henry Dewus.² It is likewise a derivative source bearing secondary information. The approximate date coincides with the newspaper's own 28 August 1936 publication date — a recognized derivative-indexing artifact rather than a specific death date stated in the obituary text. A same-person similarity score of 0.768 (strong) computed against 9VX4-1C3's tree profile confirms that the principal named in this entry is the same individual as in Q5SZ-J9LG.

### Independence Analysis and Conflict Resolution

Both entries index the same 28 August 1936 Milwaukee newspaper issue. They are **not independent**: they share the same printed source and the same informant (the unnamed obituary author). Under GPS Standard 46, they constitute one evidence unit receiving no more credibility than their strongest single member.

Conflict c_001 (resolved) adjudicated the date discrepancy between the two indexed entries. Q5SZ-J9LG's explicit "23 Aug 1936" is preferred over Q5SZ-SH2M's approximate "~28 Aug 1936" on three grounds: (1) greater precision — an explicit, unqualified date versus an approximate one; (2) the approximate date in Q5SZ-SH2M corresponds exactly to the newspaper's publication date, the hallmark of a derivative-indexing artifact in which the indexer substitutes the issue date when no explicit death date was extracted from the combined entry; and (3) a five-day interval between death (23 Aug) and newspaper publication (28 Aug) is historically normal for 1930s Milwaukee, whereas a same-day death and publication would be unusual.

### Limitations

Research has not been declared exhaustive. The following corroborating sources were identified but not yet searched:

- **Wisconsin death certificate (1936)**: Wisconsin began statewide death registration in 1907, so a death certificate for Heinrich Dewus almost certainly exists. It would supply the date and place of death as original, primary information and would identify an informant (typically a family member) whose testimony can be independently evaluated. Available through the Wisconsin Historical Society and Ancestry. Consulting this record would likely advance the conclusion to **proved**.
- **Original newspaper image** (associated with ark:/61903/1:2:QT3C-K2LH): The underlying printed obituary would confirm the stated death date and the full obituary text.
- **FindAGrave / cemetery records**: A burial record would corroborate the death date and confirm the interment location (the tree presently records burial at Pinelawn Memorial Park, Milwaukee).

### Conclusion

Heinrich Dewus **probably died on 23 August 1936 in Milwaukee, Wisconsin** (Milwaukee County). This conclusion rests on one evidence unit — two derivative-source indexed representations of the same 28 August 1936 Milwaukee newspaper obituary — evaluated as secondary information from family informants reporting to the obituary author. The explicit date (23 Aug 1936) from Q5SZ-J9LG is preferred over the approximate publication-date-derived value in Q5SZ-SH2M, as established in resolved conflict c_001. The conclusion is probable, not proved: the evidence forms a single evidence unit from derivative sources, and research has not been declared exhaustive.

---
¹ "United States, GenealogyBank Historical Newspaper Obituaries, 1815-2013", FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:Q5SZ-J9LG : accessed 2026-08-06), Entry for Henry Dewus, 28 Aug 1936.

² "United States, GenealogyBank Historical Newspaper Obituaries, 1815-2013," FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:Q5SZ-SH2M : accessed 6 August 2026), entry for Henry Dewus, death about 28 Aug 1936, Wisconsin.

(2) Wisconsin Birth Index (1946789): additional levers for both — all negative. (3) 1900 US Federal Census (1311518): five levers including child-based search using Heinrich Charles Dewus — all negative. (4) 1880 US Federal Census (6742264): one lever — negative. (5) Wisconsin State Census 1885 (1443713): three levers — all negative. (6) Wisconsin State Census 1895 (1443712): three levers — all negative. (7) Wisconsin County Marriages 1836-1911 (1803973): positive — two matching index entries confirmed Heinrich Wilhelm Johann Dewus married Auguste Bertha Friederike Arndt on 11 July 1875. Unindexed image browsing, full-text search, and non-FamilySearch repositories (Ancestry, city directories, Milwaukee vital records office) were not searched. The research has not been formally declared exhaustive.
proof_summaries.narrative_markdown:
## Did Heinrich Dewus and His Wife Augusta Have Additional Children?

**Conclusion (Probable):** Yes. Heinrich Dewus and Augusta, née Arndt, had at least two additional children — Walter (surname unstated in the obituary) and Ida (surname given as *Dewes*, a variant spelling of Dewus) — beyond the four children already documented in the family tree.

### Evidence

The primary evidence is a Milwaukee newspaper obituary of 28 August 1936, indexed at two FamilySearch entries that derive from the same newspaper publication and therefore constitute **one evidence unit** under GPS Standard 46:

1. "United States, GenealogyBank Historical Newspaper Obituaries, 1815-2013," FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:Q5SZ-J9LG : accessed 2026-08-06), Entry for Henry Dewus, 28 Aug 1936.
2. "United States, GenealogyBank Historical Newspaper Obituaries, 1815-2013," FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:Q5SZ-SH2M : accessed 6 August 2026), entry for Henry Dewus, death about 28 Aug 1936, Wisconsin.

The obituary names six surviving children: two sons (Henry C. and Walter) and four daughters (Mrs. Alma Schmidt, Miss Ida Dewes, Mrs. Adele Kniophoff, and Mrs. Hattie Henke). Four match documented Dewus children by birth records: Heinrich Charles (b. 2 Aug 1889), Alma Friedericka Wilhelmina (b. 13 Feb 1882), Adela Ulricka Augusta (b. 23 Dec 1883), and Hedwig Bertha Anna Dewus (b. 12 Sep 1885). The obituary uses the married surnames and nickname (Hattie for Hedwig) that align exactly with birth-record documentation for these four, lending internal credibility to the survivor list as a whole.

Walter and Miss Ida Dewes are the remaining two. Both are named as direct survivors — children, not grandchildren — by the obituary's phrasing and context.

*Source assessment:* The obituary is a **derivative** source (digital index of a newspaper; original image not independently examined). The survivor information is **secondary** — one or more family informants reported the names to the newspaper. The evidence is **direct** for the survivor list: the obituary asserts, in terms, that these individuals survived Heinrich Dewus as his children. Errors in obituary survivor lists occur but are uncommon when the family itself supplies the names, and the four independently verifiable names in this list all match exactly.

A corroborating evidence unit — independent in record type and separated by 61 years — establishes the couple:

3. "Wisconsin, County Marriages, 1836-1911," FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XZQS-L4R : accessed 2026-08-06), entry for Heinrich Wilhelm Johann Dewus and Auguste Bertha Friederike Arndt, 11 July 1875.
4. "Wisconsin, County Marriages, 1836-1911," FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XZQ5-DGJ : accessed 6 August 2026), entry for Heinrich Wilhelm Johan Dewus and Auguste Bertha Friederike Arndt, 11 July 1875.

These two entries index the same event (GPS Standard 46: one evidence unit). The marriage record is a **derivative** source (FamilySearch index; original register not examined); the marriage event is **primary** information for the parties present; the evidence is **direct** for the marriage. The marriage record establishes: (a) Heinrich Dewus and Augusta Arndt were legally married by 11 July 1875; (b) all six obituary children — the earliest born February 1882 — fall within this marriage; and (c) the groom's stated birthplace of Gross Turtin, Pommern, is consistent with the biographical profile for Heinrich Dewus (born circa 1850, Pomerania). The marriage record does not name any children, but it corroborates the couple as a unit and confirms that any children of Augusta Arndt born after mid-1876 were the marital children of Heinrich Dewus.

### Negative Evidence

Searches in Wisconsin Births and Christenings (1708703), the Wisconsin Birth Index, the 1880 and 1900 US Federal Censuses, and the Wisconsin State Censuses of 1885 and 1895 found no records for Walter or Ida, and no Dewus household record in any of those census years. The Dewus surname indexes under variant spellings (Due, Dew, and others) throughout Wisconsin census collections; these negatives reflect indexing limitations rather than confirmed record absence and do not contradict the conclusion.

### Tier Rationale

The preponderance favors the conclusion that Walter and Ida are children of Heinrich and Augusta Dewus. The obituary explicitly names them alongside four children whose identities are independently verifiable, and the couple's marriage is confirmed by an independent record. The conclusion does not reach **proved** because: (1) the sole direct evidence for Walter and Ida is one evidence unit (a derivative newspaper obituary with secondary information from family informants); (2) no original records independently place Walter or Ida in the Dewus household; (3) the census and birth-record negatives reflect indexing limitations rather than exhaustive record coverage; and (4) the research has not been formally declared exhaustive. Tier: **probable**.

localities.guide_markdown:
# Milwaukee, Wisconsin Locality Guide (1880–1920)

## Jurisdiction
Milwaukee County was organized in 1834 from Brown and Iowa Counties. Milwaukee City was incorporated in 1846. No boundary changes affected Milwaukee County during the 1880–1920 research window.

## Death Records
**Before 1907 (county-level registration):** Milwaukee County began recording deaths around 1852. Three indexed collections are available free at FamilySearch:
- *Wisconsin, Death Index, 1820–1907* (col. 1940759) — 435,208 records, index only
- *Wisconsin, Death Records, 1867–1907* (col. 1803975) — 184,766 records, index only
- *Wisconsin, Deaths and Burials, 1835–1968* (col. 1708699) — 24,078 records, index only

For images of the original records: FamilySearch Catalog 384199 (Milwaukee city deaths 1852–1912, with a separate index 1872–1916); Ancestry collection 61721 (Milwaukee Deaths 1854–1911, index & images, subscription). Pre-1907 index also available free at Wisconsin Historical Society.

**After 1907 (statewide registration):** Statewide compliance by 1908. Post-1907 death certificates are at the Milwaukee County Register of Deeds and Wisconsin Vital Records Office. No indexed FamilySearch collection covers 1908–1920 Milwaukee deaths — try Ancestry (collection 61721 covers to 1911) or MyHeritage Wisconsin Deaths.

**Important:** Death certificates after mid-July 1897 include birthplaces of the decedent's parents.

## Census Records
**Federal:** 1880, 1900, 1910, 1920 censuses (indexed at FamilySearch and Ancestry).
**Wisconsin State Censuses:** 1885 (col. 1443713, 407,138 records), 1895 (col. 1443712, 494,911 records), 1905 (col. 1443899, 2,228,391 records) — all indexed with images at FamilySearch. These fill the gaps between federal censuses and list all household members.

## Cemetery Records
Three Milwaukee cemeteries are indexed at FamilySearch:
- Holy Cross Cemetery, 1909–1979 (col. 3714667, 146,444 records)
- Pilgrim's Rest Cemetery, 1880–1979 (col. 3246496, 15,599 records)
- Wanderer's Rest Cemetery, 1880–1979 (col. 3326771, 30,586 records)

Additional cemeteries (Calvary 1857–1979, Forest Home 1850–1945, Union 1865–1920) are in the FamilySearch Catalog but not indexed. FindAGrave and BillionGraves also cover Milwaukee cemeteries.

## Obituaries and Newspapers
Milwaukee's large German community was served by German-language newspapers. The Milwaukee Public Library holds key obituary indexes:
- Milwaukee's German Newspapers: Index of Death Notices
- Milwaukee Sentinel Card Index, 1880–1890
- Wisconsin Necrology, 1846–1944
- Milwaukee Journal Newspaper Index, 1915–1917

Chronicling America (Library of Congress) has digitized Wisconsin newspapers free; GenealogyBank has Wisconsin newspapers 1833–2012.

## Probate Records
Milwaukee County Register in Probate has records from 1838. FamilySearch collection 1874190 (Probate Estate Files, 1848–1948, 1,399,485 images) is browse-only. Full-text-searchable Milwaukee County General Index volumes (1838–1933) are available at FamilySearch to find a name. Ancestry Wisconsin Wills and Probate Records 1800–1987 has an index with images (subscription).

## Naturalization Records
Helpful for confirming a German immigrant's identity and arrival date:
- Wisconsin, County Naturalization Records, 1807–1992 (col. 2046887, 1,530,542 records, indexed)
- Wisconsin, Milwaukee, Naturalization Index, 1848–1990 (col. 2138589, 76,410 records, indexed)

## Key Access Notes
- Milwaukee County Courthouse, 901 N 9th St, Milwaukee WI 53233: Register of Deeds has births, marriages, deaths, and land records from 1835; Register in Probate has probate records from 1838.
- Wisconsin Historical Society holds microfilms of pre-1907 vital records.
- Many Milwaukee subscription records (Ancestry, MyHeritage) may be accessed free at a FamilySearch Center or affiliate library.
